text: Among the Imperial Guards of Zhen Dan's eight directions, there is a hierarchy of rank: foremost above all stands the Dragon Emperor's Guard, warriors already exceptional among mortals, one in ten thousand, further blessed by the Dragon God and bearing the divine weapons of the Heavenly Palace—few in this world could stand against them. Next come the Jade Court Decree Guard, the Southern Beacon-Keepers, and the Long Jiang Celestial Masters, all blessed with grace beyond the mortal plane, transcendent and looking down upon all directions. As for the rest, though they possess valor to match ten thousand troops and bear the finest arms, they remain mortal flesh in the end, unable to match those ranked above them

Though the Dragon Emperor's Guard serves as the sacred watch of the Divine Palace, their authority beyond the Celestial Court far exceeds that of ordinary generals or military commissioners. In the eyes of mortals, every member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard acts in the Dragon Emperor's own stead—they may even seize control of a general's household through power or strength alone, and most of Hao Tian's generals stand before them like a mantis trying to block a chariot

Amid the ever more turbulent times, undercurrents stir within the Celestial Empire, and some even believe it teeters on the brink of collapse. As the Dragon God's champion and Grand Marshal of the God-Strategy Bureau, Yun Xiang has done everything within his power, as he sees it, to preserve the safety of Zhen Dan—but his actions have appeared to some of the Dragon-kin as overreaching, and the weight of his authority has even stirred wariness in [Jade Dragon] Yuan Bo

When the Dragon Emperor first set foot upon this land now called Zhen Dan, countless unspeakable great beasts roamed across it. Most of these creatures perished along the path of the Dragon Emperor's founding of Zhen Dan, or faded away over the long ages, but they live on forever in the legends of the people of Zhen Dan. To this day, people still believe that three guardian beasts remain in Zhen Dan, wandering the mountains and wilds, protecting Zhen Dan and upholding their ancient pact with the Dragon Emperor

As the Dragon-kin feud endlessly among themselves, the ambitions of the provincial generals swell ever greater. Some now dare to whisper in secret that the former glory of Zhen Dan vanished along with the Dragon Emperor, and that no wall, however grand, can stop the Celestial Empire from crumbling from within

The distrust between the God-Strategy Bureau and the Dragon-kin has grown ever harder to contain. The Hong Wu Overseers of the inner palace and the Raven-folk of the Jade Court are stealing intelligence from one another—Yun Xiang has even told Yuan Bo outright that the Dragon Emperor's Guard will pledge loyalty only to Hao Long himself, and the generals of every province have their own designs; the Bastion of Shang Yang stands ready to comply with your wishes. If my lord wishes to raise arms, the Hong Wu Overseers will set out at once to spread word to every province—crossing prefectures and counties, rallying rebellion, before the Dragon-kin return to court, the outcome will already be sealed!
— Li Si, Commander of the Hong Wu Overseers of Shang Yang, in secret counsel with Ye Sheng before the usurpation of Shang Yang

Ever since the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress devoted themselves wholly to their great design, the Dragon-kin have saved the Celestial Empire from ruin countless times over, even as they have, on more than one occasion, pushed Zhen Dan to the very brink of destruction. Most of the people of Zhen Dan live in a peace and prosperity that the common folk of other realms dare not even hope for, under the rule of these transcendent Dragon-kin, never tasting the cruelty of history—only those unfortunate enough to be caught in the wrath between Dragon-kin come to know just how deep a wound these dragons who look down upon the world have once inflicted upon Zhen Dan

In the 2375th year of the Imperial Calendar, three Dragon-kin led the entire Imperial Guard of their respective courts, along with vast mortal armies, into a brutal and bloody battle at Nian An Temple. Every faction had attempted to mediate before tragedy struck, but in the end all such efforts failed. The Battle of Nian An Temple ended with all three sides devastated—barely one in ten of the Imperial Guard survived, and the blood of the fallen stained the Jade River crimson. The losses were so severe that they directly shook the very foundations of dragon rule. Two years later, in 2377, the Monkey King seized control of Zhen Dan

Though martial arts and chivalry hold an unshakable and lofty place in the culture of Zhen Dan, the officials of Zhen Dan have, for the most part, never been fond of these wandering "commoners" of the martial world, seeing them as far too chaotic and uncontrollable compared to a proper standing army. And yet even they cannot deny that it is precisely these "commoners" who stepped forward and resolved the crises of Zhen Dan time and time again

Legend holds that the extraordinary might of the Dragon Emperor's Guard was personally bestowed by Hao Long centuries ago, granting them power beyond compare. But with the Dragon Emperor's departure, the Celestial Court's Imperial Guard can no longer replenish its ranks with fresh blood—these last hundred-odd guards are the final legacy of Hao Tian's blessing. Should even they one day fall in full, the very name of the Dragon Emperor's Guard will fade into just another intangible legend of Zhen Dan

Fang Wen Zi was the most powerful Astronomical Officer that Zhen Dan had seen in a hundred years; some believed his mastery of the winds of magic even surpassed that of certain Dragon-kin. During the Third Northern Campaign, Miao Ying successfully crushed dozens of khans and their vast allied hordes in the northern wastes, briefly reclaiming the East Wind Fortress that had been lost for a century. But as the army of Zhen Dan left their positions to press the pursuit, Sovereign Qing Bao's plan was set into motion: his followers rose in rebellion within the fortified encampments, several Greater Daemons were dispatched to the battlefield, and a boundless Chaos horde surged in from every direction across the wasteland—Miao Ying's legion was trapped in a hopeless situation. In this moment of crisis, Fang Wen Zi opened the Skybridge: an unbelievable miracle, for even a derelict Skybridge still echoing with the remnants of Hao Tian's power would normally require the combined effort of a hundred Astronomical Officers to activate. Perhaps even the Dragon Emperor's gaze was drawn back to the mortal world by this great feat, or perhaps this was simply his blessing all along. Miao Ying and her legion were sent back to Chang Yuan, and as the last soldier vanished at the far end of the Skybridge, Fang Wen Zi scattered upon the wind along with the miracle he had wrought, returning to the embrace of the earth

The Battle of Xuan Yuan marked the first time in the history of Zhen Dan's martial world that it formally cooperated with the imperial authorities. Over a hundred sects great and small swore a blood oath at the Grand Martial Assembly, standing forth in the moment when Zhen Dan's imperial armies were stretched thinnest, forming with flesh and blood a Great Wall of resistance at Xuan Yuan
